q: How do I cut a short local-news style report: my narration, pictures over it and a name strap for the interviewee?
a: 1. Record the narration onto its own track at the playhead (`audio.voiceover.start`) and lay it end to end. 2. Cover it with pictures on V2: target V2, video only (`timeline.setTargeting`), then Overwrite (`source.overwrite`). 3. Short interview bites on V1 between narration lines, with J and L cuts so the sound leads. 4. A lower third for the interviewee: a box pinned to the name (`graphics.pin`), left-aligned text, inside the safe margins. 5. Clean Up Voice on narration and interview (`audio.cleanupVoice`).

q: news report: the voice-over and the interview sound like two different rooms
a: Run Clean Up Voice on both (`audio.cleanupVoice`) so they land on the same loudness, then even them with Auto-Match (`essentialSound.autoMatch`); a little room tone under the narration joins them. Matching tone exactly needs the EQ controls by ear.

q: Stand-up to camera at the end of a news piece: how do I make it feel like a proper sign-off?
a: Let the reporter's last line play to the end on V1, put their name strap (lower third) up for its reading time, and end with a short Dip to Black (`sequence.applyVideoTransition` with Dip to Black) as the sign-off.

q: My night footage is full of grainy noise, how do I clean it?
a: 1. Add a node at the start of the chain (`grade.insertNode`, Insert Node Before) and raise NR luma for the grain and NR chroma for colour blotches, starting near 0.3; compare with the node off (`grade.toggleNode`). 2. For heavy noise on a static or slow shot, temporal NR on the clip (`tnr.set`): it renders at export, in the render cache and on the paused frame, not while playing. 3. Grade after the noise reduction; a little fine grain on the last node hides what's left.

q: noise reduction is making the faces look waxy
a: Lower NR luma and keep NR chroma; or clean only the dark background by adding a window to the NR node (a qualifier does not limit noise reduction), so faces keep their texture.

q: Dark concert clip from my phone: brighten it without the noise exploding.
a: Noise reduction first, on a node before the grade (`grade.insertNode`), then lift exposure gently on the next node and watch the waveform; pushing shadows hard brings the noise back. Temporal NR (`tnr.set`) helps more on slow shots than on fast stage lights.

q: How do I make the crowd cheer swell when the goal is scored?
a: 1. A crowd ambience bed under the whole match, typed Ambience (`essentialSound.setType`). 2. A separate cheer clip typed SFX lined up a few frames after the goal. 3. Ride its level up into the goal with the Audio Clip Mixer while playing (`clipMixer.set` writes Volume keyframes), and let the bed rise with it. 4. Duck any music under it or cut the music on the goal.

q: the cheer starts too suddenly and sounds pasted on
a: Start the cheer clip a little earlier with a short fade in (a Constant Power crossfade or Exponential Fade from silence), and keep the ambience bed underneath so it never jumps from nothing.

q: Make the cheer feel bigger in a highlight reel.
a: Layer two or three crowd clips on their own tracks, slightly offset, and keep voices and commentary centred; pan only the crowd layers a little left and right for width. Watch the meters so the peak stays under the limiter on the Mix.

q: How do I make a shot start as a pencil sketch and turn into the real colour footage?
a: 1. The clip on V1 and a copy on V2 above it. 2. On the copy apply Find Edges (`effects.apply`): outlines only, like a sketch. 3. Keyframe the copy's Opacity from 100 % down to 0 % over two or three seconds (`effects.toggleAnimation`, then a second value later), eased, so the colour shot shows through.

q: sketch reveal but i want ink lines to stay on top of the colour at the end
a: Keep the Find Edges copy on V2 with its Blend Mode set to Multiply: the lines draw on the colour shot underneath. For the reveal, put a second Find Edges copy (Normal) on V3 and keyframe its Opacity down, so the full sketch fades into colour with ink lines.

q: Painted look that dissolves into the real video for a travel intro.
a: Same layering with Brush Strokes on the V2 copy (Brush Size, Length; a little Blend With Original), then keyframe its Opacity down so the real shot takes over.

q: How do I make a 'previously on' recap at the start of an episode?
a: 1. Pull the key moments from earlier episodes: mark them with markers (`markers.add`) or, for dialogue, select the lines in the transcript and extract them (`transcript.extract`). 2. Cut them short and fast in order, one line each. 3. A title card 'Previously on…' at the start. 4. Music bed under it, ducked under the lines (`essentialSound.generateDucking`). 5. Dip to Black into the new episode.

q: recap clips have different loudness from different episodes
a: Select the recap's dialogue clips and Auto-Match them (`essentialSound.autoMatch`), or run Clean Up Voice on them; music and effects get their own types.

q: Recap for a vlog series where the shots come from different cameras.
a: Copy one grade across the scene and check for the odd one out, or match each shot to a reference still with Shot Match, so the recap doesn't jump in colour between clips.

q: My podcast guest recorded remotely is much quieter and noisier than me. How do I even them out?
a: 1. Put each person on their own track and type both clips Dialogue (`essentialSound.setType`). 2. Run Clean Up Voice on the guest (`audio.cleanupVoice`): it measures the clip and sets noise reduction and loudness. 3. Auto-Match both (`essentialSound.autoMatch`) so they land on the same loudness. 4. Mix to the platform target at the end.

q: guest audio has an echo from their room
a: Raise Reduce Reverb in Essential Sound's Repair section (DeReverb) on the guest clip, or Voice Isolation for noise and room together; stop before the voice turns thin.

q: Remote interview: the guest's voice sometimes peaks and sometimes drops away.
a: A compressor on the guest (Essential Sound Dynamics, moderate ratio) evens it; ride the leftover dips with Volume keyframes from the Audio Clip Mixer (`clipMixer.set`).

q: How do I animate a highlighter marker sweeping across a word in my title?
a: 1. The title on the top track. 2. On the track below, a rectangle graphic over the word (`graphics.newRectangle`), yellow. 3. On the rectangle's clip apply Crop and keyframe Right from 100 % to 0 % (`effects.toggleAnimation`), Linear, so it sweeps in. 4. Set its Blend Mode to Multiply so the text stays dark on it.

q: highlighter animation on a few different words, same every time
a: Make one, then save its effects as a preset (`presets.save`) with Anchor to In Point so the sweep keeps its timing; apply it to the next rectangle (`presets.apply`).

q: Underline that draws itself under a key phrase.
a: A thin rectangle graphic under the phrase, Crop Right keyframed from 100 % to 0 % with Ease Out, timed to the voice saying the phrase; keep it inside the safe margins.

q: How do I add a progress bar along the bottom of my video that fills as it plays?
a: 1. A rectangle graphic across the bottom edge (`graphics.newRectangle`), a few pixels tall, inside the safe area, stretched to the length of the sequence. 2. Apply Crop to it and keyframe Right from 100 % at the start to 0 % at the end (`effects.toggleAnimation`), interpolation Linear (`effects.setInterpolation`) so it fills at a steady speed. 3. Optionally a darker full-width rectangle under it as the track.

q: progress bar speeds up and slows down instead of steady
a: The keyframes are eased; right-click them and choose Linear (`effects.setInterpolation`) so the bar fills at a constant speed.

q: Progress bar split into chapter segments for a tutorial.
a: Put a marker at each chapter start (`markers.add`), then place thin divider rectangles on the bar at those times, and keep the fill as one Crop-keyframed rectangle under them; the same markers export as YouTube chapters.

q: How do I bring out the Milky Way in my night-sky timelapse?
a: 1. Noise reduction first on a node at the start of the chain (`grade.insertNode`; NR luma and chroma); temporal NR on the clip (`tnr.set`) helps on slow skies. 2. Next node: contrast around a low pivot so the stars and the band separate from the sky. 3. A qualifier or gradient window on the sky only, so the ground stays dark. 4. Neutral or slightly cool balance.

q: stars flicker between frames in my night timelapse
a: Revolution has no deflicker effect yet. Temporal noise reduction (`tnr.set`) smooths fine frame-to-frame changes but not big brightness pulses; for a few bad frames, keyframe Exposure (Lumetri) or Offset to even them out; Frame Blending at a slightly changed speed mixes neighbouring frames. Best fixed at the shoot with manual exposure.

q: Night sky looks orange from city light pollution.
a: Balance the sky first: a gradient window on the sky with the light-pollution glow cooled (Gain / Temperature towards blue) on its own node, so the foreground keeps its look.
